messages:
alex: Quick follow-up to the lease/abuse thread. We saw revoked tenants spinning across scheduler shards and getting new leases before revokes propagated. Result: eviction churn and noisy metrics.
jo: Are revokes only written to KV and read lazily? That's the classic window.
alex: Yep. KV tombstones + eventual reads. Need something that minimizes reads on the happy path but prevents fast regain after a revoke.
samir: Idea: revocation records with a monotonic seq + tiny severity flag, cached at edges. On a miss, instead of blocking, move the tenant to a probation fallback (reduced throughput) while we async-fetch the record. Also emit a best-effort fanout to primes caches.
jo: That avoids adding KV latency to normal admissions. What about false positives and retracts?
alex: Retracts should be another record with higher seq (clear intent). Edges compare seqs, so ordering is safe. For appeals, ops can post a retract which sets seq and clears severity; automated appeals go to probation.
samir: Metrics to add before rollout: revoke-seq bumps, cache hit %, async-KV read latency, new-lease-after-revoke rate, probation throughput.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: cache+probation fallback to 20% of edge schedulers at 03:00 UTC for 2h.
jo: Action items: alex -> small micro-RFC with seq format and TTL suggestions (15/30/45s); samir -> prototype cache + async fetch + fanout stub; ops -> write retract/appeal playbook and dashboards.
alex: Let's keep first rollout probation-only (no hard-deny) and ensure ops are on-call. We'll reconvene after canary for numbers.
